name: Blake Huber
current_role: Former state chair, Libertarian Party of Colorado
bio: Denver political activist and election-reform advocate who describes himself as longtime in that work. He has served as a Libertarian Party state chair, served in the Kansas National Guard and U.S. Navy Reserve, and has 30+ years in management. Earlier runs include Approval Voting Party VP (2016), Colorado Secretary of State (2018), and president (2020, 2024).

platform.point: Advocates approval voting so voters can support multiple candidates.
Supports regulation reform that reduces unnecessary burdens on small businesses.
Names immigration reform as a priority.

economy.evidence: Supports regulation reform that reduces unnecessary burdens on small businesses.

immigration.evidence: Names immigration reform as a priority without specifics.

notes: Little public detail found; campaign website not verified.

name: Jeff Peckman
bio: Author, entrepreneur and consultant who calls himself a solutionist. He is a transcendental meditation practitioner and a longtime advocate for government disclosure of UFO evidence. He won the Unity Party primary in June 2026. His campaign centers on a philosophy he calls coherence.

platform.point: Proposes a Chief Coherence Officer and a partnership to apply coherence-based technologies in state government.
Calls for a moratorium on new AI data center construction.
Says methane-to-graphene production could meet Colorado's emissions goals within two years without subsidies.
Called ICE actions domestic terrorism and suggests exporting coherence technologies to address root causes of migration.
Proposes a state Extraterrestrial Affairs Commission.

immigration.evidence: Criticized ICE actions as domestic terrorism and proposes addressing root causes of migration.

energy.evidence: Says graphene and plasma technologies could meet emissions goals without tax-funded incentives or subsidies.

tech.evidence: Calls for a moratorium on new AI data center construction in Colorado.

notes: Campaign website URL not verified. Some proposed technologies lack independent scientific verification (noted by CPR).

name: Charles W. Burkett
bio: Four-term mayor of Surfside, Florida, who led the town through the 2021 Champlain Towers South collapse. A real estate entrepreneur, he is running for governor with no party affiliation.

platform.point: Proposes phasing out taxes on homesteaded primary residences over time.
Wants more competition among financially strong insurers.
Says legal immigration is good and uncontrolled, illegal immigration is bad.
Opposes data centers in Florida and favors a county referendum.
Prefers renovation over new construction and opposes Manhattanization of South Florida.

economy.evidence: Proposes gradually eliminating taxes on homesteaded primary residences and more insurer competition.

immigration.evidence: Says legal immigration is good while uncontrolled, unvetted, illegal immigration is bad.

tech.evidence: Opposes data centers in Florida and says counties should vote in a referendum on them.

education.evidence: Calls for real education rather than factory-style educational warehousing; no structural position stated.

notes: Education score is from a slogan-level statement.

name: Paul Sand
bio: Retired software engineer and antiques shop owner in White Bird, Idaho. He served on the White Bird City Council from 2007 to 2017 and is making his second run for governor. His site says he opposes all political parties, including the Libertarians.

platform.point: Wants counties and local government to be the top layer, with few statewide offices.
Says state income and sales taxes would go away.
Says all illegal immigrants need to be sent home and opposes public benefits for any immigrant.
Opposes sending money and weapons to any country.
Opposes privatizing public lands.
Strongly opposed to abortion and to legalizing narcotic drugs.

economy.evidence: Says state income and sales taxes would go away and supports substantial cuts to state agencies.

liberty.evidence: Strongly opposed to abortion and to legalizing narcotic drugs.

immigration.evidence: Says all illegal immigrants need to be sent home and opposes public benefits for any immigrant.

foreign.evidence: Opposed to sending any money and weapons to any country.

notes: Sources are his campaign site as summarized by a fetch tool.

name: Cathy White
bio: Production worker with about 40 years in a factory who describes herself as not a professional politician. She ran for lieutenant governor on the Working Class Party ticket in 2022 and is the party's 2026 nominee for governor, with Cathy Permut as running mate.

platform.point: Campaign emphasizes jobs, wages, inflation, caregiving, public infrastructure and opposition to war.

notes: Pages with her own detailed statements could not be read (403 or thin); no domains scored. Website is the party's Maryland page.

name: Doug Campbell
bio: Retired professional engineer and substitute high school teacher from Ferndale who joined the Green Party in 2000. He declines corporate PAC money and is running with Bobbie Clay for lieutenant governor.

platform.point: Names affordability, energy and education as top priorities.
Proposes direct government hiring on a Green New Deal model and universal basic income.
Would close Line 5, move utilities to municipal agencies and expand solar and EVs.
Would end the charter system and fund schools statewide.
Says immigrants built the United States and wants residents protected from federal overreach.

economy.evidence: Proposes direct government hiring on a Green New Deal model and says job incentives become corporate welfare.

immigration.evidence: Says immigrants built the United States and that wage suppression is not caused by immigration.

energy.evidence: Would close Line 5, convert utilities to municipal agencies, install solar and promote electric vehicles.

education.evidence: Wants to eliminate the charter system and adopt statewide school funding.

notes: Source is his Vote411 answers as summarized by a fetch tool.

name: Chuck Conboy
bio: Papillion, Nebraska resident running for U.S. Senate on the America First Party ticket against Republican Pete Ricketts and independent Dan Osborn.
notes: Little public information found. Party platform (limited government, no new wars) not attributed to him personally, so not scored.

name: Veronica Fernandez
bio: Long Valley, New Jersey resident, former property-casualty insurance underwriter, and co-owner of a small electrical contracting business with her husband. She is affiliated with the League of Women Voters and has run for Senate (2020), House (2022) and Assembly (2023).

platform.point: Wants Citizens United overturned by constitutional amendment.
Supports Medicare for All.
Proposes abolishing ICE with fast-tracked citizenship.
Backs tuition-free public colleges and fully funded public schools.
Opposes U.S. arms shipments to Israel.
Supports meaningful, common-sense gun laws.

welfare.evidence: Supports Medicare for All and would sign on to Sanders' S.1506.

immigration.evidence: Proposes abolishing ICE with fast-tracked citizenship pathways.

foreign.evidence: Opposes U.S. arms shipments to Israel.

education.evidence: Backs tuition-free public colleges and fully funded public schools.

notes: Positions come from an aggregator (smarter.vote) summarizing her campaign material; her own site not verified.

name: Sevier White
bio: Libertarian nominee in the November 2026 special election for the Oklahoma U.S. Senate seat vacated by Markwayne Mullin. He previously ran for U.S. House as a Libertarian in 2000 and 2016.
notes: Little public information found; League of Women Voters guide reported no positions from him.

name: Gary Lyndon Dye
bio: Portland-born technical consultant with degrees in chemical engineering, an MBA, and math and physics. He previously worked as a gas measurement engineer at NW Natural. He ran for U.S. Senate in 2020 and U.S. House in 2018 and 2024 as a Libertarian.
notes: Portland Civic Lab reports no 2026 policy statements; website is a 2020 campaign site. No domains scored.

name: Dean Brewer
bio: Knoxville resident originally from Lenoir City with no prior political office, who qualified as an independent by petition. He proposes a program giving homeless veterans counseling, housing and skilled-trade training.

platform.point: Proposes housing, counseling and on-the-job trade training for homeless veterans.

notes: Little public information found; only slogan-level and veterans statements.

name: Lauren Pinkston (Forward Party)
bio: Seventh-generation Tennessean from Columbia, mother of four, former public school teacher and Lipscomb assistant professor with a Clemson doctorate. She started businesses employing human trafficking survivors in Thailand and Laos. Running as an independent endorsed by the Forward Party.

platform.point: Says she is more fiscally conservative but dedicated to social safety nets.
Supports shifting Education Freedom Scholarship growth toward early childhood education rather than vouchers.
Wants safe, well-funded schools and fewer benchmark tests.

economy.evidence: Describes herself as more fiscally conservative but very dedicated to social safety nets.

welfare.evidence: Says she is dedicated to social safety nets.

education.evidence: Wants well-funded schools and would shift scholarship budget growth to early childhood education rather than vouchers.

notes: Facebook and Instagram handles came from search results, not opened.

name: Ted Brown
bio: Retired independent insurance adjuster born in Steubenville, Ohio, with a UCLA political science degree. He has chaired the Libertarian Party of California and been vice chair of the Travis County party. He won about 267,000 votes in his 2024 Senate run.

platform.point: Wants to abolish the federal income tax and the IRS.
Wants to eliminate the Department of Education.
Proposes an Ellis Island-style legal immigration system.
Wants to withdraw from foreign conflicts and alliances like NATO.

economy.evidence: Wants to abolish the federal income tax, dismantle the IRS and sharply cut spending.

immigration.evidence: Proposes an Ellis Island-style legal immigration system.

foreign.evidence: Wants to withdraw the U.S. from foreign conflicts and alliances like NATO.

education.evidence: Wants to eliminate the federal Department of Education.

notes: X handle came from search results, not opened.

name: Peter Williams
bio: Agriculturist and tree farmer from Lettsworth, Louisiana, and 1980 University of Southwestern Louisiana graduate. He previously ran for Senate (2016), agriculture commissioner (2019) and the 6th district (2024), and switched to the Republican Party in 2025.
notes: No issue positions found; smarter.vote reports none documented.

name: Rufus H. Craig, Jr.
bio: Baton Rouge attorney and former chairman of the Libertarian Party of Louisiana. He ran for this seat in 2022, taking 13 percent against Garret Graves.

platform.point: Pledged support for transparent elections and against efforts to disenfranchise citizens.

notes: Only an elections pledge found; no scorable domain.

name: Joe Jock
bio: Green Party nominee in Michigan's 3rd district (Grand Rapids and Muskegon area), nominated at the July 2026 convention. He describes himself as a working-class Michigander.
notes: Search summary of his Ballotpedia survey mentions universal healthcare, worker ownership and privacy from mass surveillance, but Ballotpedia is blocked and no readable source was found, so not scored.

name: Linda Rayburn
bio: Detroit-based caregiver and substitute teacher who attended Henry Ford Community College. She previously ran for Michigan House (2024, 6.0 percent) and State Senate (2022).

platform.point: Earlier statement says racism, poverty and an unjust criminal justice system break communities apart.

notes: Little current policy detail found.

name: Kevin Vayko
bio: Environmental engineer with a 2011 Michigan Tech degree who has worked at Aura Environmental. He was the Libertarian nominee for this seat in 2024 and is again in 2026.

platform.point: Supports restrictions in cases such as rape and irreparable maternal harm, leaving the decision to states.
Disagreed that forgiveness unfairly burdens others, arguing employers share responsibility.
Supports ESG ratings for public investment, citing climate concern.

liberty.evidence: Supports abortion restrictions with exceptions and says the decision is left to the states.

energy.evidence: Supports ESG ratings for public investment, saying the climate crisis gets little attention.

notes: iVoterGuide answers were about 60 percent blank. Scores are weak.

name: Ryan Teasdale
bio: Loan processor from Waterford, Michigan, and Green Party nominee in the 11th district, nominated unopposed at the April 2026 state convention.

platform.point: Runs on abolishing ICE.

immigration.evidence: Runs on a Green Party platform that includes abolishing ICE.

notes: Single position from an aggregator.

name: Raelyn Light
bio: Green Party candidate in Michigan's 13th district, facing Democrat Donavan McKinney and Republican T.P. Nykoriak.
notes: Did not answer the Vote411 questionnaire; little public information found.

name: Russell Best
bio: Independent American Party nominee in Nevada's 4th district. A former Navy storekeeper discharged for medical reasons, he owns an independent mortgage company in northern Nevada and has run for office several times.
notes: No campaign positions found.
